title: Influence of drying and rehydration on the emulsifying ability of cellulose nanofibers derived from a lignocellulosic residue (soybean hulls)
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Lignocellulosic biomass is produced in large amounts globally and it represents an underexploited source of cellulose. Nanocelluloses refer to cellulose isolated fibers with at least one dimension on the nanoscale. Important issues must be taken into consideration for the successful revalorization of lignocellulose into nanocelluloses applications. The first involves the use of proper treatments for the deconstruction of the complex lignocellulose structure. The second involves obtaining dehydrated and water redispersible materials by reducing the hornification of nanocelluloses during drying. The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of drying and resuspensions methods on water dispersibility of cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) obtained from soybean hulls by chemical–mechanical treatment, as well as evaluate the extent to which it may compromise its original properties and functionality as Pickering emulsifiers.

RESULTS

Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis demonstrated the presence of cellulose and, to a minor extent, hemicellulose in CNFs. The addition of different concentrations of glycerol was used to avoid hornification during oven drying of CNFs, and different resuspension methods were evaluated after drying (magnetic stirring and ultrasonication) to improve the dispersibility of CNFs. Although the presence of glycerol improved water dispersibility of CNFs, ultrasonication generates water rehydrated CNFs with conserved morphology and increased resuspension stability. CNFs subjected to drying and ultrasonication were also capable of forming and stabilizing oil-in-water Pickering emulsions during long time storage.

CONCLUSION

This research highlights the possibility of obtaining dehydrated nanocellulose from lignocellulosic biomass (soybean hulls), with conserved functionality for a wide variety of applications, such as emulsifiers for the food industry. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
